model: EWWD-VZ water-cooled screw chiller (Daikin Applied Europe)
applies_to: Daikin Applied Europe EWWD-VZ, EWWH-VZ and EWWS-VZ water-cooled inverter screw chillers (MicroTech, software "Adam").
summary: The European EWWD/EWWH/EWWS VZ water-cooled screw chillers use a MicroTech controller running the "Adam" software. BACnet IP or BACnet MS/TP is added with a plug-in POL908 or POL904 module, or on MicroTech 4 as an onboard software option. The list covers unit enable, mode and network setpoints, evaporator and condenser water temperatures, per-circuit refrigerant data, compressor VFD values and a large set of individual alarm BVs, plus warning/problem/fault index and code AVs.
notes: This is the Daikin Applied Europe guide; it is a different object list from the US MicroTech chiller documents.
The guide covers MicroTech III and MicroTech 4 controllers with one object list.
Object names use dots (e.g. C1.Comp1.Starts) and are kept as printed.
Access "W Prio 8" in the guide is shown as C; plain "W" is shown as W.

One MV row printed with name and instance "MISSING" (a second measurement-unit setpoint) is left out. BV 904 is printed for both Unit.OFFRestartBoardOffline and Unit.OFFMarineBoardOffline; the second is listed without an instance.
Default device instance 1 applies to BACnet IP; on the MS/TP module it is derived from the production number.

integration.summary: Select network control at the unit (CtrlSource BI 3 then reads Network), enable the chiller with UnitEnableStp, and write the mode, cool setpoint and capacity limit at priority 8. Monitor unit status, leaving water temperature, the alarm output and the fault code.

minimum_points.name: UnitModeSetpointNetwork
minimum_points.why: Ice / cool / heat / pursuit mode command

minimum_points.name: NetworkCoolTempSetpoint
minimum_points.why: Leaving water cool setpoint from the BMS

minimum_points.name: CtrlSource
minimum_points.why: Shows whether network control is active

integration.enable: CtrlSource (BI 3) reads 0 = Network / 1 = Local and is read-only over BACnet, so network control has to be selected at the unit; the guide does not describe that step. With network control active the BMS writes UnitEnableStp (BV 2) = Enable, then the mode (MV 3) and network setpoints.
setup: BACnet IP comes from the POL908 module or, on MicroTech 4, the onboard BACnet IP software option (enabled under Commissioning > Configuration > Software Options with an unlock password).
BACnet MS/TP comes from the POL904 module or the onboard BACnet MS/TP software option.
BACnet IP defaults: device instance 1, UDP port 47808, DHCP off; set Apply Changes = Yes after editing, which restarts the controller.

BACnet MS/TP module defaults: MAC address 24, 38400 baud, Max Master 127, Max Info Frames 1; the device instance is derived from the production number and date code. Cycle power after changing the address.
EDE files are regenerated each time the BACnet server starts and can be downloaded by FTP from the POL908; re-export them after any configuration change.
gotchas: The guide marks the enable, alarm-reset, mode and main network setpoint objects as written at priority 8 (access C here); write them at priority 8.
Compressor start counters and run-hour AVs are marked writable; don't write them from the BMS.
Alarms come as Warning, Problem and Fault index/code AVs (900-905); decode them with the alarm code table in section 5.1 of the guide.
MV 4 Units selects metric or English units for the BACnet values; set it once, not cyclically.
